name: Republican Party of Wisconsin
subject: A MESSAGE FROM NATIONAL COMMITTEEWOMAN PAM TRAVIS
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE REPUBLICAN PARTY OF WISCONSIN** NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE
body:
[](https://republicanpartyofwisconsin.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fkrdykk-didthutlhu-r/) Republicans of Wisconsin,Sitting in the RPW War Room on election night was tough. The disappointment felt overwhelming, and I know you felt it too. That loss is especially hard because I know how much we put into trying to win: every shift, conversation, dollar raised, and hour spent supporting our party and candidates. I'm personally grateful to each of you for all you gave.History has made midterm elections difficult for the party in power. We worked against those headwinds and sought to earn voters' confidence. We recruited and supported great candidates, organized across our communities, raised money, reached voters, and worked to protect the integrity of our elections. That effort mattered. The results may not be what we hoped for, but they don't erase the work or the capacity Wisconsin Republicans built together.We have too much at stake, and Wisconsin is too important to walk away from. As Senator Johnson has said, "This country is way too precious to give up on." I believe that. My dad didn't raise a quitter, and I'm committed to Wisconsin and to the work ahead. I hope you'll stay with me in that work.The principles our party stands for--individual freedom, personal responsibility, opportunity, and a government accountable to the people--are part of a larger American promise. Our Founding Fathers risked their lives and livelihoods to pursue self-government and liberty, hoping to secure those ideals for future generations. We have a responsibility to carry that work forward across the country while building a stronger Republican Party here in Wisconsin. Speaker Mike Johnson has spoken about passing faith and freedom on to the next generation. That work begins close to home: with neighbors talking to neighbors, volunteers organizing, and county parties equipped to reach voters year after year.My goal is to build lasting infrastructure in Wisconsin and make sure county parties have the resources, training, and support to succeed. I believe our county members are the heart of this movement and can help revitalize it.Months ago, I sought to share a strategy and practical plan with RPW leadership to lay that foundation for success. I still believe this work is needed: strengthening county parties, developing new leaders, and equipping volunteers--the backbone of our movement--with the tools to organize in every corner of Wisconsin. I hope we can make it a priority together.The people closest to the work must shape it. You know how to reach me, and I'll keep listening to your ideas, concerns, and recommendations. I'm grateful to be working alongside you as we build a stronger future for our party. With gratitude and resolve, Pam Travis
